question.problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ k \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =1\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (-1\cdot k)+3\cdot (2\cdot 3) \\  & =-2-2k+18 \\  & =16-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 16-2k & =0 \\ 2k & =16 \\ k & =8\end{aligned}
$$
